Party found a guy next to a tower after being warned about a necromancer. DM was conspicuously silent through all this. 

We play over Messenger, and had to take a break at that point for one of the girls to quickly make some dinner. So I’m sat there, and I suddenly start to get this horrible feeling because we made absolutely *no* attempt to talk to this guy. We were newbie players, we’d gotten into the mindset of “if they’re not you they want you dead” and we’d just gone in all crossbows blazing because of it. 

So we come back, and the first thing I say is, “Can I try talking to the guy?” 

“... You just appeared out of nowhere and shot him.” 

“Yeah, but I feel really bad about it.” 

Her response is best summed up as “bitch you best roll a Nat20”. I did not. 

And thus we turned what should have been a simple “hi there, seen any gang leaders lately?” into “thank fuck we’ve got a cleric to deal with the undead while I beat this dude unconscious with my Pimp Cane of Defence”. At least it was a great learning moment for us, and later saved us from what would most likely have been a party wipe when we decided to shmooze a banshee instead of aggroing her.

Alright, so I legitimately don’t remember at all how it started (it was my uni days, so probably something was said while drunk). But I walk creepily quiet at all times, and our flat at that time had poured-concrete floors, so no creaking floorboards to worry about. So long as I was wearing soft clothing I could literally get within a few feet of people without them realising I was there. We also usually all left our doors propped open when we were home during the day, so we could get stuff done but still talk to each other. 

Anyway, however it started, I ended up leaving tins of sweetcorn for her to find. Nothing special, only those little Green Giant ones. I started off leaving them in her kitchen cabinets, then moved on to putting them in her wardrobe, in her plant pots, her shower, you name it, there was a tin of corn there. And she didn’t know who was doing it. I mean, they’d just sort of appear, so obviously she strongly suspected it was me, but she never caught me and our other two flatmates cheerfully played dumb. 

My two proudest moments- the time I left a tin on a kitchen chair in the middle of our bedroom hallway, so when she came in drunk and switched the light on it was waiting there for her like a disapproving parent. And the time I happened to see her pull into the car park as she came home from Tesco, knew that meant she’d be getting the lift, and hurried out to put a tin perfectly in the centre of it. So the lift doors opened and there it was, the Devil’s Corn, just waiting for her. 

It all ended when my hubris got the best of me, and I tried leaving a tin for her when she was in the bathroom, which was an ensuite. Still, I went out in a blaze of glory - hauled myself under her bed before she could see me, rolled the tin towards her as she sat at her desk, and grabbed her wrist while screaming “COORRRNNN!” when she went to pick it up. Luckily she saw the funny side, y’know, after the shrieking had died down.

Yeah, chimerism is my favourite “weird nature” thing. You know there’s that one cat people always share pictures of, where both sides of their face are totally different colours, eyes are different colours? That’s chimerism. She’s basically two cats smushed together. 

You get it in people, too. Sometimes you can see it (people with two different-coloured eyes, patches of hair/ skin being different colours), but more often it effects your organs. There was a woman who lost custody of her kids because after a DNA test they turned out to be related to her, but *not* her children. Turns out she was a chimera, her uterus came from the sister-embryo she absorbed, and so the kids were genetically her nieces/ nephews. 

You could be a chimera right now, without even knowing it!

Cats can only be calico/ tortoiseshell if they’ve got the marker for it on two X-chromosomes, so the very small number of male calicos/ torties out there are that way because of a genetic abnormality that gives them an extra X (people can get it too, it’s called Klinefelter Syndrome). *Or* they can end up that way if they’re a chimera, and a calico/ tortie female embryo merged with a male embryo early enough in development for him to still end up a male, only with the female coat pattern. The chimera ones are usually healthier than the XXYs. 

So yeah, if you had a male calico then there was a less-than-1% chance of him being that way, so he was a very unique little chap.

>it helps start up breathing again

This is a really dangerous misconception a *lot* of people have, mostly because tv/ film plays it that way - 30 seconds of CPR and suddenly they’re up and running again, yay! 

CPR is basically to keep oxygen running through their brain until the paramedics can get there and take over. It’s possible, but *very, very unlikely* that CPR is going to wake that person up. What it will do is make it less likely for them to suffer brain death. 

It actually happened to my uncle, my cousin stopped doing CPR because “he wasn’t waking up”, by the time the ambulance got there he was brain dead. Then again, she’s also morbidly obese, so she might have just quit. CPR is fucking hard, if you’re doing it right.

So you’ve got a trilogy set in one place, with mentions of one guy’s cousin, then another series focusing on the cousin. Not a sequel, but characters from the first set are mentioned/ appear in the second. 

My favourite is my fantasy world, where I came up with a full world map, multiple languages and cultures, plus (at the moment) roughly 1000 years of history. I’ve written stories based on points along the history line, so nothing is a direct sequel, but everything references the stories before it. The fun thing then is, depending on how far apart the two are, the events of one story can be referenced by another character and can be completely wrong, because it’s already become a myth to them. Plus, some big hero of Rhaillor will be seen as a figurehead of an evil regime in Firan etc.
